newsitem.title: NEW ZEALAND: Air NZ, Ansett, Singapore alliance in fares deal.
newsitem.headline: Air NZ, Ansett, Singapore alliance in fares deal.

text.p: Air New Zealand, Ansett International, Ansett Australia and Singapore Airlines on Wednesday launched a shared fares structure less than a week after the formation of a three-way commercial alliance.

In a statement from the New Zealand carrier, the group said the Escapade programme would allow passengers to buy air travel across their combined networks by "distance value" in order to make long-distance flying costs simpler and more flexible.
"Global travel need not be complicated," said Grant Lilly, Air New Zealand's general manager, regional sales and marketing.

The plan is built around three types of fares on an upward sliding scale, Oceania for bands of maximum distance up to 15,000 air miles (24,000 km), Pacific for journeys up to 22,000 miles (35,200 km) and Round the World for up to 29,000 miles (46,400 km).

The fares would be locally priced in each country of sale, but a single price would cover any point-to-point journey in the distance band, regardless of which partner airline is used. Additional travel distance can be bought in pre-set lots.

Although the alliance of Australian regional operator Ansett (and its fledgling international arm), Air New Zealand and Asian giant Singapore Airlines is not based on equity ties, the four last Friday agreed comprehensive code- and cost-sharing links.
